caveats: Velocity-free tau: BIND's 'kSZ' is the electron-column optical depth, not a velocity-weighted temperature; a real Delta T_kSZ is unbuilt (needs a DMO-velocity surrogate; Phase-3 kill-gate G3, not attempted).

TNG model space only: the 256-node Sobol design samples TNG-like feedback parametrizations only; the paper's thesis is explicitly about model-space vs parameter-space tension, not a test of non-TNG subgrid physics.

Mass floor 1e13 for painted halos: the TNG300 lightcone halo catalog floor is M200>=1e13; the DESI ELG-host regime (~1e12.5) sits below it. Low-mass (1e12-1e13) reuse via patch cross-matching recovers only a partial sample (28.7% within the 4xR200 production paste, 51.6% at the full 6.25 Mpc/h patch footprint); the uncaptured ~48% are field halos far from any >=1e13 cluster (captured halos have median host distance 1.87-1.9 Mpc/h, i.e. near-cluster not field), though an environment-bias check found the captured sample's f~gas is representative (near-host vs field 0.408 vs 0.409, <0.3% difference).

Satellite/miscentering effects: the tSZ y-CAP profile SHAPE (not amplitude) is not compared to data because the real photometric-LRG stack is smoothed by miscentering + photo-z LOS spread + the ACT beam (modelled/marginalised by the survey, not by BIND) -- only the 1-halo y-CAP amplitude is compared. Similarly the kappa comparison is restricted to the 1-halo scale (theta<3') because BIND's isolated per-halo patch carries no 2-halo term.

y-map normalization is already physical (Compton-y needs no extra 1/a^2 weighting) per standing project convention; not independently re-derived within the ksz-desi-act sources but consistent with all y-map usage in this project.

Open provenance gap: ksz_fgas_confront.py (the D1 '0% coverage' result) reads f_gas_500 directly from integrated.parquet with no visible background-subtraction step in that file; whether the parquet column already carries the LOS-contamination fix later applied in halo_atlas.py (2026-06-15) could not be confirmed from the sources -- flag for the verifier, do not assert the D1 Sobol-wide numbers (f_gas~0.11-0.15) and the corrected bg-subtracted single-run numbers (f_gas,500=0.076) are on the same footing.

GNFW (alpha,beta) point comparison is explicitly flagged invalid: alpha~0.2 is a near-singular corner of the fixed gamma=-0.5,x_c=0.7 GNFW form, degenerate with the fixed core; only the profile-overlay + outer slope beta is meaningful.

The kSZ-inferred f_gas computed by forward-integrating the Hadzhiyska/Ried-Guachalla GNFW density table is unphysical as transcribed (gives BGS_all -> 0); do not reproduce this calculation, use the CAP-ratio comparison or the paper's own reported f_gas table instead.

The original 3-probe (kappa,tau,y) thermodynamic decomposition and its 'too much gas, not too hot' conclusion is RETRACTED after the tSZ mass-selection bug fix; no valid T_e/heating-vs-ejection decomposition currently exists in the sources.

Posterior covariances are approximate: the joint multi-M*-bin CAP posterior uses a diagonal covariance treating nested M* bins as independent (optimistic); the multiprobe kSZ+tSZ forecast uses a 'realistic AR(1) aperture covariance' (better, but still not the survey's published bin-bin covariance) -- both flagged as open TODOs.
Compare like with like: BIND f_gas = total gas; eROSITA = hot X-ray gas; kSZ = total electrons -- the X-ray band is a lower envelope on true gas content, not a literal kSZ target.

The central-M* selection proxy (painted Stars channel within ~50 kpc/h) has not been independently validated against TNG Subfind stellar mass at fiducial (DMO<->hydro match) -- listed as an open TODO.

sigma_v=300 km/s (T_CMB sigma_v/c=2727 microK) is used throughout the (now-dropped) raw CAP-tau conversion; an earlier draft used an erroneous 1176 microK from a digitization slip -- moot for the final paper since the raw CAP-tau panel was dropped in favor of the sigma_v-free f~gas ratio, but worth a footnote if any raw tau-CAP number is ever shown.
